meta.title: ThoxOS Ginux Edition 0.2.0
meta.subtitle: Azure images with ThoxOS Desktop: cold-built Ginux kernel, cloud host kernel, three TXF looks, real screenshots
meta.owner: Odette Lark, memory-sync node and fleet librarian
meta.closing: Research preview. Not for production use.

lede: ThoxOS Ginux Edition now builds Azure VM images. The desktop image boots a Debian 13 host with the Azure cloud kernel into ThoxOS Desktop, the TXF 5.2 desktop with three looks, and each RDP user runs ThoxOS on the Ginux kernel from the dock. Booted in QEMU the way Azure provisions a VM, it passed 23 of 23 checks, and every screenshot here comes from that run. Azure Virtual Desktop cannot host Linux session hosts, so the image follows Microsoft's golden-image flow as a standard Azure VM. Nothing has run on Azure yet.

blocks.text: Host images move to 0.2.0; the Ginux guest stays 0.1.0. One Dockerfile builds every host root, with a target (KnightHub or Azure) and a desktop option (headless or ThoxOS Desktop).

sections.heading: Azure Virtual Desktop and this image

blocks.text: Microsoft's guide prepares a Windows golden image for AVD host pools. AVD session hosts run Windows 11 or 10 Enterprise and Windows Server only, so a Linux image cannot join a host pool. The ThoxOS image follows the same golden-image steps and deploys as a standard Azure VM reached over RDP.

blocks.title: Security type
blocks.text: Standard, not Trusted Launch: the systemd-boot loader is unsigned. A signed loader is queued before Trusted Launch can be claimed.

rows: Desktop VHD booted in QEMU like Azure provisions it (cloud-init, NoCloud seed)
23 of 23 checks: SSH after 43 s, cloud-init done, no failed units, per-machine keys and machine ID, Hyper-V initrd, agent settings

blocks.text: Sixteen defects surfaced in the build and bench runs and were fixed before the final images, among them a 300 s initramfs sleep from rootdelay, a GTK theme setting that made the desktop session spin at full CPU, and a machine ID that every VM would have shared (VALIDATION.md D-01 to D-16). The 0.1.0 KnightHub image very likely carries that last defect too.
Real captures from the final desktop VHD booted in QEMU with software emulation and reached over RDP. They show the shipped image, not Azure.

items: Build the VHD: installer/build-host-image.sh --target azure --desktop desktop (about 2 minutes with a warm Docker cache).
Publish: azure/publish-image.sh --vhd build/azure/thoxos-ginux-azure-desktop-0.2.0.vhd --resource-group thoxos-images --location eastus. It prints the image version ID.
Deploy: az deployment group create with azure/azuredeploy.json, the image version ID, allowedSourceCidr set to your address and an administrator password.
Connect with RDP to the VM's DNS name; pick a look; open ThoxOS on Ginux from the dock.
Optional: set aiUpstream, aiAuth, aiApiKey and aiModel to route thox ask to a hosted model.

blocks.title: Exposure
blocks.text: SSH and RDP open only to the one source range you pass; there is no default. Ginux has no security audit: keep it a research VM.

A second runtime answered the same request in pull request #2: an Ubuntu 24.04 marketplace host with a bootstrap artifact, a private VM behind NAT, Trusted Launch, a kernel startup patch with five fixes plus an Azure profile patch, and no desktop. The two records agree that AVD cannot host Ginux and that nothing ran on Azure. They differ on image strategy, security type, exposure and the kernel patch set. RECONCILIATION_2026-10-29.md lists each point for a ruling; neither record was changed to match the other.
